topics.title: June Version MMM
topics.text:
Me and my co-host, AWaltz would like to present to you the MMM (MathArt4's Monthly Mock)! Please read all of this before taking the test.

Problem Information:

This mock is made up of 6 problems.

Scoring Information:

These 6 problems will be scored on a scale of 0-1.

Difficulty:

These problems are approximately AMC 8 level. If you want to see the problems, you can click on the google docs link below, which will lead you to the test.

Submitting your solutions:

Your submissions will be accepted and graded from now to June 8th. Please private message me AND AWaltz with your solutions.

Timing:

You have 30 minutes to complete all of the test.

Finding an error:

If you have an error, please private message me and I will get back to you as soon as possible.

Signups:

Signup below in signup tags.

Calculators:

Calculators are allowed for certain problems. For the June Monthly, these questions are 2,4, and 6. For the other questions, there is no need to use a calculator.

Submitting Problems:

We are accepting 1 user written problem for the July Monthly, this user's problem will appear in the July Monthly (they will receive credit). Please private message me with your problem as well as an answer to your problem. A problem without an answer will be disqualified. Also, make sure the problem is AMC 8 level.

If you have questions, please post them below.

V1: https://docs.google.com/document/d/1MnXMDDgQPb8uLY4MgRQ4YJCKgZxMq0Bqq-f80NlPgj4/edit

Enjoy!

~MathArt4 and AWaltz

topics.title: Area of Trapezium ("New" Way!)
topics.text:
ProofNote:

This proof only works for non-parallelogram trapeziums!

(Make sure you see why!)



Let $AB = b_1$ and $CD = b_2$.

Also let $r_1 = b_1/2$ and $r_2 = b_2/2$.



As $\angle VAB = \angle VCD$ and $\angle AVB = \angle CVD$, $\triangle VAB \sim \triangle VCD$ by AA similarity.



Let $d$ denote the perpendicular from point $V$ to segment $\overline{AB}$



So, $d/(d+h) = r_1/r_2$.

Therefore, $d = (r_1 h)/(r_2 - r_1)$



\begin{align*}
    [VCD] &= \frac{1}{2} \cdot b_2 \cdot \left(\frac{r_1 h}{r_2 - r_1} + h\right) \\
    &= \frac{1}{2} \cdot b_2 \cdot \left(\frac{r_2 h}{r_2 - r_1}\right) \\
    &= \frac{b_2}{2} \cdot \frac{r_2 h}{r_2 - r_1}
\end{align*}

\begin{align*}
    [VAB] &= \frac{1}{2} \cdot b_1 \cdot \left(\frac{r_1 h}{r_2 - r_1}\right) \\
    &= \frac{b_1}{2} \cdot \frac{r_1 h}{r_2 - r_1}
\end{align*}

Therefore:



\begin{align*}
    [ABCD] &= \left(\frac{1}{2} \cdot b_2 \cdot \frac{r_2 h}{r_2 - r_1}\right) - \left(\frac{1}{2} \cdot b_1 \cdot \frac{r_1 h}{r_2 - r_1}\right) \\
    &= \frac{h}{2(r_2 - r_1)} \cdot (b_2 \cdot r_2 - b_1 \cdot r_1) \\
    &= \frac{h}{2(r_2 - r_1)} \cdot (2 r_2^2 - 2 r_1^2) \\
    &= \frac{h}{r_2 - r_1} \cdot (r_2^2 - r_1^2) \\
    &= \frac{h}{r_2 - r_1} \cdot (r_2 - r_1) (r_2 + r_1) \\
    &= h (r_2 + r_1) \\
    &= h \left(\frac{b_1 + b_2}{2}\right) \\
    &= \boxed{\frac{1}{2} \cdot h \cdot (b_1 + b_2)}
\end{align*}

Q.E.D




InspirationI was asked to find a formula for the volume of a general frustum, and the frustum look ALOT like a trapezium, so I thought the same technique MIGHT apply for the area of a TRAPEZIUM.

And guess what? It DID apply!




Reply if you like it!

Mathew wants to put numbers on the toy cars in his

collection (he has more than 100 of them). To do this, he

buys stickers bearing the digits 0, 1, 2, 3, 4, 5, 6, 7 or 8;

the digit 6 can represent a 9 by being used upside down.

He has 20 stickers of each digit, so 180 stickers altogether.

If Mathew numbers his cars from 1 upwards, what will

be the first number that he cannot make?

topics.title: Some people...
topics.text:
There were 31 people at the masked ball.

Emma danced with 8 boys, Jade danced with 9 boys,

Chloe danced with 10 boys, etc.... up to Manon, the last

girl, who danced with all the boys that were there.

How many boys were there ?

topics.title: A strange problem... :)
topics.text:
We are in the year 2016, and Cedric’s age is a factor of

2016. If Cedric adds up all the multiples of his age that are

less than 365, he arrives at the year he was born.

In which year was he born?

topics.title: A cryptarithm
topics.text:
A cryptarithm is a substitution code where different

letters represent different digits, two digits can never be

represented by the same letter and numbers cannot start

with a 0.

DU + CAFE = NOIR

This cryptarithm has more than one solution. But for the

solution where CAFE is the smallest possible number,

what number is NOIR ?

topics.title: The four cyclists (A curious problem)
topics.text:
The four cyclists (A curious problem)

Each of four cyclists rode round a different circle.One at the rate of six miles

an hour, the third at the rate of twelve miles an hour ,the fourth at the rate

of fifteen miles an hour.They started off at twelve o'clock at the centre.They

agreed to ride until all met in the centre for the fourth time.The distance round

each circle was one-third of a mile.

When did the four cyclists meet for the fourth time?

topics.title: k June Version MMM
topics.text:
Me and my co-host, AWaltz would like to present to you the MMM (MathArt4's Monthly Mock)!   Please read all of this before taking the test.

Problem Information:

This mock is made up of 6 problems. These 6 problems will be questions that require a solution to be written to receive full credit.

Scoring Information:

These 6 problems will be scored on a scale of 0-3. The rubric is on the front page of the test.

Difficulty:

These problems are approximately AMC 8 level. If you want to see the problems, you can click on the google docs link below, which will lead you to the test.

Submitting your solutions:

Your submissions will be accepted and graded from now to June 8th. Please private message me AND AWaltz with your solutions.

Timing:

You have 90 minutes to complete all of the test. We think that 15 minutes per question is reasonable.

Finding an error:

If you have an error, please private message me and I will get back to you as soon as possible.

Signups:

There is no need to sign up. You can just take the test.

Calculators:

Calculators are allowed for certain problems. For the June Monthly, these questions are 2,4, and 6. For the other questions, there is no need to use a calculator.

 Submitting Problems:

We are accepting 1 user written problem for the July Monthly, this user's problem will appear in the July Monthly (they will receive credit). Please private message me with your problem as well as an answer to your problem. A problem without an answer will be disqualified. Also, make sure the problem is AMC 8 level.

If you have questions, please post them below.

Link to test: https://docs.google.com/document/d/1MnXMDDgQPb8uLY4MgRQ4YJCKgZxMq0Bqq-f80NlPgj4/edit

Enjoy!

~MathArt4 and AWaltz

topics.title: Hard probability question
topics.text:
In Lietopia, everyone lies with a $99\%$ probability and tells the truth with a $1\%$ probability. In Lietruthopolis, everyone both lies and tells the truth with a $50\%$ probability. In a Lietruthopolis-Lietopia party, two people are asked if they like a new movie. They both say "yes".

What is the probability that they both like the new movie?



Sorry if this is too hard, but it's a spinoff of an ocelot-centered problem that I made while going to bed. Please move if necessary.
